q: The Gurmukhi script, in which the Punjabi language is written, was standardised by:
e: The Gurmukhi script, in which Punjabi is written in India, was standardised by Guru Angad Dev, the second Guru of the Sikhs.

q: Which of the following is NOT an official language of the State of Sikkim?
e: Hindi is not an official language of Sikkim; the official languages of the State include Nepali, Lepcha and Bhutia (Sikkimese), besides English.

q: The Assamese language belongs to which group of the Indo-Aryan family of languages?
e: Assamese belongs to the Eastern group of the Indo-Aryan family of languages, along with Bengali and Odia.

q: Which of the following languages was included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution as originally enacted?
e: Sanskrit was one of the languages included in the Eighth Schedule as originally enacted; Sindhi, Konkani and Nepali were added to the Schedule subsequently.

q: Which of the following is one of the official languages of the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir under the Jammu and Kashmir Official Languages Act, 2020?
e: Under the Jammu and Kashmir Official Languages Act, 2020, Kashmiri is one of the official languages of the Union Territory, along with Dogri, Urdu, Hindi and English.

q: The office of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities was set up in the year:
e: The office of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities was set up in the year 1957 to investigate and safeguard the interests of the linguistic minorities in India.

q: Under the National Education Policy, 2020, the three-language formula for school education:

options.B: Makes the study of Hindi compulsory in all the States
options.C: Applies only to the schools run by the Central Government
options.D: Will continue to be implemented, and no language will be imposed on any State

e: Under the National Education Policy, 2020, the three-language formula will continue to be implemented, with greater flexibility, and no language will be imposed on any State.

q: In Hindi, the term used for 'Official Language' is:
e: Rajbhasha is the Hindi term used for 'Official Language', the language used for the official purposes of the Union and the States; Rashtrabhasha means national language, a term not used in the Constitution.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In a Central Government office notified under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976, an employee who has acquired working knowledge of Hindi can be required to do noting and drafting in Hindi on the subjects specified in the notification.
2. Such an employee can also be required to furnish an English translation of the noting made by him in Hindi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is true: in a notified office, an employee with working knowledge of Hindi can be required to do noting and drafting in Hindi on the subjects specified in the notification. Statement 2 is false: he cannot be required to furnish an English translation of it.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Budget" is:
e: Bajat is the prescribed Hindi equivalent of 'Budget', the annual statement of the estimated receipts and expenditure of the Government.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Grant" is:
e: Anudan is the prescribed Hindi equivalent of 'Grant', the money sanctioned or allotted for a specific purpose; Bajat means budget and Rin means a loan.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Revenue" is:
e: Rajaswa is the prescribed Hindi equivalent of 'Revenue', the income of the Government derived from taxes and other sources.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Act" is:
e: Adhiniyam is the prescribed Hindi equivalent of 'Act', a law enacted by the Legislature; Adhyadesh means an Ordinance and Vidheyak means a Bill.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Ordinance" is:
e: Adhyadesh is the prescribed Hindi equivalent of 'Ordinance', a temporary law promulgated by the President or a Governor when the Legislature is not in session.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Amendment" is:
e: Sanshodhan is the prescribed Hindi equivalent of 'Amendment', a change or correction made in a Bill, an Act or any document.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Bill" (a legislative proposal) is:
e: Vidheyak is the prescribed Hindi equivalent of 'Bill', the draft of a proposed law placed before the Legislature for enactment.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Constitution" is:
e: Samvidhan is the prescribed Hindi equivalent of 'Constitution', the fundamental law of the country according to which the Government is run.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Schedule" is:
e: Anusuchi is the prescribed Hindi equivalent of 'Schedule', an appendix attached to an Act or to the Constitution containing detailed lists and particulars.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Translation" is:
e: Anuvad is the prescribed Hindi equivalent of 'Translation', the rendering of matter written in one language into another language.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Resignation" is:
e: Tyagpatra is the prescribed Hindi equivalent of 'Resignation', the letter by which an employee voluntarily gives up his post or office.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Superannuation" is:
e: Adhivarshita is the prescribed Hindi equivalent of 'Superannuation', meaning retirement on attaining the prescribed age; Sevanivritti is the general term for retirement.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Dearness Allowance" is:
e: Mahangai Bhatta is the prescribed Hindi equivalent of 'Dearness Allowance', the allowance paid to employees to compensate them for the rise in the cost of living.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Service Book" is:
e: Seva Pustika is the prescribed Hindi equivalent of 'Service Book', the official record maintained for every employee containing his service particulars.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Advertisement" is:
e: Vigyapan is the prescribed Hindi equivalent of 'Advertisement', a public announcement made to promote or notify something; Suchna means information or notice.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Estimate" is:
e: Aakalan is the prescribed Hindi equivalent of 'Estimate', an approximate calculation of cost, quantity or expenditure made in advance.

q: The Official Language Resolution, embodying the policy for the progressive use of Hindi for the official purposes of the Union, was adopted by Parliament in the year:
e: The Official Language Resolution, embodying the policy for the progressive use of Hindi for the official purposes of the Union, was adopted by Parliament in the year 1968.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The use of Hindi in the proceedings of the Uttarakhand High Court has been authorised by the Governor of the State with the previous consent of the President.
2. The use of Hindi in the proceedings of the Chhattisgarh High Court has been authorised by the Governor of the State with the previous consent of the President.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is false: the use of Hindi in the proceedings of the Uttarakhand High Court has not been so authorised. Statement 2 is true: the use of Hindi in the proceedings of the Chhattisgarh High Court has been authorised by the Governor with the previous consent of the President.

q: Which of the following is NOT an official language of the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir under the Jammu and Kashmir Official Languages Act, 2020?
e: Punjabi is not an official language of the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir under the 2020 Act; the recognised languages are Kashmiri, Dogri, Urdu, Hindi and English.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Bhoti is one of the official languages of the Union Territory of Ladakh.
2. Purgi is one of the official languages of the Union Territory of Ladakh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both statements are true: Bhoti and Purgi are both among the languages recognised as official languages of the Union Territory of Ladakh.

q: Urdu has been declared as the second official language of the State of:
e: Urdu has been declared as the second official language of Telangana, in addition to Telugu, the official language of the State.

q: The language of the subordinate (district) courts in the State of Haryana is:
e: The subordinate (district) courts in Haryana conduct their work in Hindi, which is the official language of the State.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the Union Territory of Puducherry, Telugu may be used for official purposes in the Yanam region.
2. In the Union Territory of Puducherry, Malayalam may be used for official purposes in the Mahe region.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both statements are true: in the Union Territory of Puducherry, Telugu may be used for official purposes in the Yanam region and Malayalam in the Mahe region, in keeping with the languages of the adjoining areas.

q: The Eighth World Hindi Conference was held in the year 2007 at:
e: The Eighth World Hindi Conference was held in the year 2007 at New York, in the United States of America.

q: The first Hindi daily newspaper, 'Samachar Sudha Varshan', was published in the year 1854 from:
e: 'Samachar Sudha Varshan', the first Hindi daily newspaper, was published in the year 1854 from Calcutta.

q: Who among the following is regarded as the father of modern Hindi literature?
e: Bharatendu Harishchandra is regarded as the father of modern Hindi literature for his pioneering contribution to modern Hindi prose, poetry and drama.

q: 'Alam Ara', the first Indian talkie film released in the year 1931, was made in the:
e: 'Alam Ara', the first Indian talkie film released in the year 1931, was made in the Hindi language.

q: According to the Census of India, 2011, the fifth most widely spoken language (mother tongue) in India is:
e: According to the Census of India, 2011, Tamil is the fifth most widely spoken mother tongue, after Hindi, Bengali, Marathi and Telugu.

q: Under the National Education Policy, 2020, wherever possible, the medium of instruction should be the mother tongue/local language until at least:
e: Under the National Education Policy, 2020, wherever possible, the medium of instruction should be the mother tongue or local language until at least Class V.

q:
Consider the following statements about 'Udant Martand', the first Hindi newspaper:
1. It was a weekly newspaper.
2. It was printed in the Devanagari script.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both statements are true: 'Udant Martand', the first Hindi newspaper, was a weekly newspaper, and it was printed in the Devanagari script.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. English is one of the official languages of the State of Sikkim.
2. English is one of the official languages of the State of Mizoram.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both statements are true: English is one of the official languages of the State of Sikkim, and it is also one of the official languages of the State of Mizoram.

q: Urdu has been declared as the second official language of the State of:
e: Urdu has been declared as the second official language of Telangana, in addition to Telugu, the official language of the State.

q: Under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the 'general orders' issued by a Central Government office are required to be issued in:

options.D: The regional language of the State where the office is located

e: Under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the general orders issued by a Central Government office are required to be issued in both Hindi and English.

q: The passenger tickets issued by the Indian Railways are printed in:
e: The passenger tickets issued by the Indian Railways are printed in Hindi and English, so that passengers of both language groups can read them.

q: Which of the following languages is NOT included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution?
e: Rajasthani is not included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, whereas Dogri, Bodo and Santhali are among the twenty-two languages included in it.

q: The Nagari Pracharini Sabha, founded in the year 1893 for the promotion of the Devanagari script, was established at:
e: The Nagari Pracharini Sabha, founded in the year 1893 for the promotion of the Devanagari script and the Hindi language, was established at Varanasi.

q: 'Rekhta' was the earlier name by which the following language was commonly known:
e: Rekhta was the earlier name by which Urdu was commonly known in the early period of its literary development.

q: The 'Ramcharitmanas' of Goswami Tulsidas is written in:
e: The 'Ramcharitmanas' of Goswami Tulsidas is written in Awadhi, the literary language of the eastern Hindi region.

q: 'Dakkhini', an early literary form of the Hindi-Urdu speech, developed mainly in the region of:
e: Dakkhini, an early literary form of the Hindi-Urdu speech, developed mainly in the Deccan region of southern India.

q: The Lepcha language of Sikkim is written in the script known as:
e: The Lepcha language of Sikkim is written in its own script, which is known as the Rong script.

q: At present, the Manipuri language is written for official purposes mainly in the:
e: At present, the Manipuri language is written for official purposes mainly in the Bengali script, though its own script, Meitei Mayek, is also being revived and promoted.

q: The Bhojpuri language was traditionally written in the:
e: The Bhojpuri language was traditionally written in the Kaithi script, which was widely used for legal, administrative and commercial writing in Bihar and eastern Uttar Pradesh.

q: The Modi script was traditionally used for writing the:
e: The Modi script was traditionally used for writing Marathi; it is a cursive script suited to rapid writing.

q: The Sharada script was traditionally used for writing the:
e: The Sharada script was traditionally used for writing the Kashmiri language in the Kashmir region.

q: The first Indian leader to address the United Nations General Assembly in Hindi was:
e: Atal Bihari Vajpayee was the first Indian leader to address the United Nations General Assembly in Hindi, which he did as India's External Affairs Minister.

q: The number of official languages of the United Nations is:
e: The United Nations has six official languages, namely Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish; Hindi is not among them.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Attendance" is:
e: Upasthiti is the prescribed Hindi equivalent of 'Attendance', meaning the presence of an employee at his place of duty.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Income Tax" is:
e: Aay Kar is the prescribed Hindi equivalent of 'Income Tax', the tax levied on the income of persons; Aay alone means income.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Registration" is:
e: Panjikaran is the prescribed Hindi equivalent of 'Registration', the act of recording a name or particulars in an official register.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Reservation" is:
e: Aarakshan is the prescribed Hindi equivalent of 'Reservation', the setting apart of posts, seats or facilities for specified categories of persons.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Competent Authority" is:
e: Saksham Pradhikari is the prescribed Hindi equivalent of 'Competent Authority', the authority empowered under the rules to take a decision in a matter.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Vigilance" is:
e: Satarkta is the prescribed Hindi equivalent of 'Vigilance', meaning watchfulness exercised to prevent corruption and irregularities in administration.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Code" is:
e: Samhita is the prescribed Hindi equivalent of 'Code', a systematic collection of rules or laws relating to a subject.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Regulation" is:
e: Viniyam is the prescribed Hindi equivalent of 'Regulation', a rule made under an Act for carrying it into effect; Niyamavali means a set or collection of rules.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Recommendation" is:
e: Sifarish is the prescribed Hindi equivalent of 'Recommendation', the action of suggesting or commending a person or a course of action for consideration.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Warning" is:
e: Chetavani is the prescribed Hindi equivalent of 'Warning', a formal caution administered to an employee or a person for a lapse.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Demi-Official Letter" is:
e: Ardh Shaskiya Patra is the prescribed Hindi equivalent of 'Demi-Official Letter', a letter written in a semi-official and personal style to draw special attention to a matter.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Medical Certificate" is:
e: Chikitsa Praman Patra is the prescribed Hindi equivalent of 'Medical Certificate', a certificate issued by a medical practitioner about the health or fitness of a person.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Identity Card" is:
e: Parichay Patra is the prescribed Hindi equivalent of 'Identity Card', a card issued to establish the identity of its holder.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Priority" is:
e: Prathmikta is the prescribed Hindi equivalent of 'Priority', the precedence given to one matter over others in the order of disposal.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Expenditure" is:
e: Vyay is the prescribed Hindi equivalent of 'Expenditure', the money spent for a purpose; Aay means income and Anudan means a grant.

q: The Eighth Schedule of the Constitution is referred to in which of the following Articles of the Constitution?
e: The Eighth Schedule of the Constitution is referred to in Articles 344 and 351, which relate to the Commission and Committee on Official Language and the directive for the development of the Hindi language.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The number of mother tongues returned in the raw returns of the Census of India, 2011 was 19,569.
2. The number of languages each spoken by 10,000 or more persons, as per the Census of India, 2011, is 121.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both statements are true: the number of mother tongues returned in the raw returns of the Census of India, 2011 was 19,569, and the number of languages each spoken by 10,000 or more persons is 121.

q: According to the Census of India, 2011, which of the following languages included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution has the smallest number of speakers?
e: According to the Census of India, 2011, Sanskrit has the smallest number of speakers among all the languages included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution.

q: In terms of the total number of speakers in the world, the language which ranks third, after English and Mandarin Chinese, is:
e: In terms of the total number of speakers in the world, Hindi ranks third, after English and Mandarin Chinese.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Fourth World Hindi Conference was held at Port Louis (Mauritius) in the year 1993.
2. The Ninth World Hindi Conference was held at Johannesburg (South Africa) in the year 2012.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both statements are true: the Fourth World Hindi Conference was held at Port Louis (Mauritius) in the year 1993, and the Ninth World Hindi Conference was held at Johannesburg (South Africa) in the year 2012.

q: The Sixth World Hindi Conference was held in the year 1999 at:
e: The Sixth World Hindi Conference was held in the year 1999 at London, in the United Kingdom.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Dakshin Bharat Hindi Prachar Sabha was founded by Mahatma Gandhi at Madras in the year 1918.
2. The Rashtrabhasha Prachar Samiti was established at Wardha in the year 1936.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both statements are true: the Dakshin Bharat Hindi Prachar Sabha was founded by Mahatma Gandhi at Madras in the year 1918 for the propagation of Hindi in South India, and the Rashtrabhasha Prachar Samiti was established at Wardha in the year 1936.

q: The official language of the State of Madhya Pradesh is:
e: Hindi is the official language of the State of Madhya Pradesh.

q: The official language of the State of Himachal Pradesh is:
e: Hindi is the official language of the State of Himachal Pradesh.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Bhutia is one of the official languages of the State of Sikkim.
2. Lepcha is one of the official languages of the State of Sikkim.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both statements are true: Bhutia is one of the official languages of the State of Sikkim, and Lepcha is also one of the official languages of the State.

q: The language of the subordinate (district) courts in the State of Uttarakhand is:
e: The language of the subordinate (district) courts in the State of Uttarakhand is Hindi, the official language of the State.

q: The Annual Assessment Report on the implementation of the Annual Programme for the progressive use of Hindi, which is laid before both Houses of Parliament, is prepared by:

options.C: The Committee of Parliament on Official Language

e: The Annual Assessment Report on the implementation of the Annual Programme for the progressive use of Hindi, which is laid before both Houses of Parliament, is prepared by the Department of Official Language.

q: The first province in India to adopt Hindi in the Devanagari script in place of Persian for court work, in the year 1881, was:
e: Bihar was the first province in India to adopt Hindi in the Devanagari script in place of Persian for court work, which it did in the year 1881.

q: The Kashmiri language belongs to which of the following groups of the Indo-Aryan family of languages?
e: The Kashmiri language belongs to the Dardic group of the Indo-Aryan family of languages, spoken in the north-western part of the subcontinent.

q: The Bodo language, included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, belongs to which family of languages?
e: The Bodo language, included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, belongs to the Tibeto-Burman family of languages.

q: Which of the following languages is popularly known as the 'Italian of the East'?
e: Telugu is popularly known as the 'Italian of the East' because of its melodious sound, as its words generally end in vowel sounds.

q: The Hindi Teaching Scheme for imparting in-service Hindi training to Central Government employees was introduced in the year:
e: The Hindi Teaching Scheme, for imparting in-service Hindi training to Central Government employees through the Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya courses, was introduced in the year 1955.

q: Which of the following languages does NOT belong to the Dravidian family of languages?
e: Marathi does not belong to the Dravidian family; it is an Indo-Aryan language, whereas Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam are all Dravidian languages.

q: 'Pariksha Guru' (1882), regarded as the first novel in Hindi, was written by:
e: 'Pariksha Guru' (1882), regarded as the first novel in Hindi, was written by Lala Srinivas Das.

q: The real name of Munshi Premchand, the celebrated Hindi novelist, was:
e: The real name of Munshi Premchand, the celebrated Hindi novelist, was Dhanpat Rai Srivastava; Premchand was his pen name.

q: The celebrated Hindi magazine 'Saraswati' was edited for a long period by:
e: The celebrated Hindi magazine 'Saraswati' was edited for a long period by Mahavir Prasad Dwivedi, who used it to shape and standardise modern Hindi prose.

q: Before the rise of Khari Boli as the literary language, the principal literary language of the Hindi-speaking region in the medieval period was:
e: Before the rise of Khari Boli as the literary language, Braj Bhasha was the principal literary language of the Hindi-speaking region in the medieval period.

q: 'Padmavat', the celebrated Sufi epic poem, was composed by:
e: 'Padmavat', the celebrated Sufi epic poem, was composed by Malik Muhammad Jayasi.

q: The epic poem 'Prithviraj Raso' is traditionally attributed to:
e: The epic poem 'Prithviraj Raso' is traditionally attributed to Chand Bardai, the court poet of Prithviraj Chauhan.

q: The poet who is credited with the earliest compositions in Hindavi (early Khari Boli) is:
e: Amir Khusro is credited with the earliest compositions in Hindavi, the early form of Khari Boli, in which he wrote riddles and verses.

q: The development of modern Khari Boli prose in Hindi in the early nineteenth century is associated with:

options.D: The Central Hindi Directorate, New Delhi

e: The development of modern Khari Boli prose in Hindi in the early nineteenth century is associated with the Fort William College at Calcutta, where prose texts in the language were prepared.

q: 'Thirukkural', the celebrated classical work in Tamil, was authored by:
e: 'Thirukkural', the celebrated classical work in Tamil, was authored by Thiruvalluvar.

q: Rabindranath Tagore's 'Gitanjali' was originally written in the:
e: Rabindranath Tagore's 'Gitanjali' was originally written in the Bengali language and was later translated by the poet himself into English.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Honorarium" is:
e: Maanadeya is the prescribed Hindi equivalent of 'Honorarium', a payment made for services rendered, usually of a special or occasional nature.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Remuneration" is:
e: Parishramik is the prescribed Hindi equivalent of 'Remuneration', the payment received in return for work or services; Vetan means salary.
